messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

Source link: https://ndownloader.figstatic.com/files/4230046
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1021/ac201416j

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Droplet-Based Pyrosequencing Using Digital Microfluidics (on-chip PCR amplification, magnetic-bead-based purification, and cyclic dNTP pyrosequencing with real-time luminescence detection)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Genomic DNA (C. parapsilosis genomic DNA purified from culture, PCR template)
  - Primer Mix (ITS1 forward primer 5'-Bio-tccgtaggtgaacctgcgg-3' and ITS2 reverse primer 5'-gctgcgttcttcatcgatgc-3', 0.24 uM each, amplifying a 229 bp fragment)
  - PCR Reagent (20 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.4, 1.5 mM MgCl2, 50 mM KCl, 0.2 mM dNTPs, 1 U Platinum Taq polymerase)
  - Magnetic Beads (streptavidin-coated magnetic beads for capture of the biotinylated PCR product)
  - Wash Buffer (used in repeated merge-and-split wash cycles to purify bead-bound ssDNA)
  - Sequencing Primer (hybridizes to the bead-bound single-stranded template for pyrosequencing, e.g. P6/P6-1-style primer)
  - Enzyme Mix (ATP sulfurylase/luciferase/apyrase pyrosequencing enzyme cocktail with adenosine 5' phosphosulfate and luciferin)
  - dNTP Reagents (dATP, dCTP, dGTP, dTTP dispensed sequentially in a defined nucleotide addition order)

STEPS:
1. PCR setup: combine genomic DNA template with the ITS1/ITS2 primer mix and PCR reagent (Tris-HCl/MgCl2/KCl/dNTP/Taq polymerase buffer) to form the amplification reaction droplet.
2. Hot start: incubate the reaction at 95 C for 2 minutes.
3. Amplification: cycle 40 times through 95 C for 15 s (denaturation) and 60 C for 30 s (anneal/extend).
4. Final extension: incubate the reaction at 72 C for 1 minute.
5. Bead capture: merge the amplified, biotinylated PCR product droplet with a streptavidin magnetic bead droplet to capture the product.
6. Magnetic bead washing: repeatedly merge a fresh wash buffer droplet with the bead-bound droplet and split off the wash droplet, cycling to purify the captured single-stranded template (demonstrated over hundreds of wash cycles with no observable bead loss).
7. Primer annealing: merge the washed, bead-bound ssDNA with sequencing primer and incubate at 65 C to hybridize the sequencing primer.
8. Enzyme addition: merge the annealed template droplet with the ATP-sulfurylase/luciferase/apyrase enzyme mix to prepare the pyrosequencing reaction droplet.
9. Cyclic nucleotide dispensing and detection: in a defined dispensing order, sequentially merge each dNTP droplet (dATP, dCTP, dGTP, dTTP) with the reaction droplet and measure the real-time luminescence (photons/sec) generated by each addition; a rising signal indicates nucleotide incorporation into the growing strand, while a flat/background signal indicates a non-incorporating ("bkgd") addition, together revealing the template sequence.

module fluorescence

manifest genomic_dna
manifest primer_mix
manifest pcr_reagent
manifest wash_buffer
manifest magnetic_beads
manifest sequencing_primer
manifest enzyme_mix
manifest datp_reagent
manifest dctp_reagent
manifest dgtp_reagent
manifest dttp_reagent

instructions:

dna = dispense 1 units of genomic_dna
primers = dispense 1 units of primer_mix
mix1 = mix dna with primers for 15s
pcr_reagent_drop = dispense 1 units of pcr_reagent
pcr_rxn = mix mix1 with pcr_reagent_drop for 15s

heat pcr_rxn at 95c for 120s

repeat 40 times {
    heat pcr_rxn at 95c for 15s
    heat pcr_rxn at 60c for 30s
}

heat pcr_rxn at 72c for 60s

beads = dispense 1 units of magnetic_beads
capture = mix pcr_rxn with beads for 60s

repeat 5 times {
    wash = dispense 1 units of wash_buffer
    capture = mix capture with wash for 30s
    dispose capture
}

seq_primer = dispense 1 units of sequencing_primer
anneal = mix capture with seq_primer for 30s
heat anneal at 65c for 120s

enzyme = dispense 1 units of enzyme_mix
seq_rxn = mix anneal with enzyme for 15s

repeat 10 times {

    datp = dispense 1 units of datp_reagent
    seq_rxn = mix seq_rxn with datp for 5s
    a_signal = detect fluorescence on seq_rxn for 60s

    dctp = dispense 1 units of dctp_reagent
    seq_rxn = mix seq_rxn with dctp for 5s
    c_signal = detect fluorescence on seq_rxn for 60s

    dgtp = dispense 1 units of dgtp_reagent
    seq_rxn = mix seq_rxn with dgtp for 5s
    g_signal = detect fluorescence on seq_rxn for 60s

    dttp = dispense 1 units of dttp_reagent
    seq_rxn = mix seq_rxn with dttp for 5s
    t_signal = detect fluorescence on seq_rxn for 60s

    if (a_signal <= 1000) {
        dispose seq_rxn
    }
}

dispose seq_rxn

main:
	dna1[0] = dispense(genomic_dna)
	primers1[0] = dispense(primer_mix)
	mix11[0] = mix(dna1[0], primers1[0]) @ 15.0SECOND
	pcr_reagent_drop1[0] = dispense(pcr_reagent)
	pcr_rxn1[0] = mix(mix11[0], pcr_reagent_drop1[0]) @ 15.0SECOND
	heat(pcr_rxn1[0]) @ 95.0CELSIUS @ 120.0SECOND
bsbbr_2_h:
	PHI REPEAT_401 = {REPEAT_400,REPEAT_402}
	PHI pcr_rxn2 = {pcr_rxn1,pcr_rxn2}
	if REPEAT_401[0] > 0	|	true: jump bsbbr_3_t	|	false: jump bsbbr_4_f
bsbbr_3_t:
	heat(pcr_rxn2[0]) @ 95.0CELSIUS @ 15.0SECOND
	heat(pcr_rxn2[0]) @ 60.0CELSIUS @ 30.0SECOND
	REPEAT_402[0] = REPEAT_401[0] - 1
bsbbr_4_f:
	heat(pcr_rxn2[0]) @ 72.0CELSIUS @ 60.0SECOND
	beads1[0] = dispense(magnetic_beads)
	capture1[0] = mix(pcr_rxn2[0], beads1[0]) @ 60.0SECOND
bsbbr_5_h:
	PHI REPEAT_51 = {REPEAT_50,REPEAT_52}
	PHI wash1 = {wash0,wash2}
	PHI capture2 = {capture1,capture3}
	if REPEAT_51[0] > 0	|	true: jump bsbbr_6_t	|	false: jump bsbbr_7_f
bsbbr_6_t:
	wash2[0] = dispense(wash_buffer)
	capture3[0] = mix(capture2[0], wash2[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	dispose(capture3[0])
	REPEAT_52[0] = REPEAT_51[0] - 1
bsbbr_7_f:
	seq_primer1[0] = dispense(sequencing_primer)
	anneal1[0] = mix(capture2[0], seq_primer1[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	heat(anneal1[0]) @ 65.0CELSIUS @ 120.0SECOND
	enzyme1[0] = dispense(enzyme_mix)
	seq_rxn1[0] = mix(anneal1[0], enzyme1[0]) @ 15.0SECOND
bsbbr_8_h:
	PHI REPEAT_101 = {REPEAT_100,REPEAT_102}
	PHI dctp1 = {dctp0,dctp2}
	PHI datp1 = {datp0,datp2}
	PHI c_signal1 = {c_signal0,c_signal2}
	PHI dttp1 = {dttp0,dttp2}
	PHI a_signal1 = {a_signal0,a_signal2}
	PHI g_signal1 = {g_signal0,g_signal2}
	PHI dgtp1 = {dgtp0,dgtp2}
	PHI t_signal1 = {t_signal0,t_signal2}
	PHI seq_rxn2 = {seq_rxn1,seq_rxn7}
	if REPEAT_101[0] > 0	|	true: jump bsbbr_9_t	|	false: jump bsbbr_12_f
bsbbr_9_t:
	datp2[0] = dispense(datp_reagent)
	seq_rxn3[0] = mix(seq_rxn2[0], datp2[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	a_signal2[0] = detect(fluorescence, seq_rxn3[0]) @ 60.0SECOND
	dctp2[0] = dispense(dctp_reagent)
	seq_rxn4[0] = mix(seq_rxn3[0], dctp2[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	c_signal2[0] = detect(fluorescence, seq_rxn4[0]) @ 60.0SECOND
	dgtp2[0] = dispense(dgtp_reagent)
	seq_rxn5[0] = mix(seq_rxn4[0], dgtp2[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	g_signal2[0] = detect(fluorescence, seq_rxn5[0]) @ 60.0SECOND
	dttp2[0] = dispense(dttp_reagent)
	seq_rxn6[0] = mix(seq_rxn5[0], dttp2[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	t_signal2[0] = detect(fluorescence, seq_rxn6[0]) @ 60.0SECOND
	if a_signal2[0] <= 1000	|	true: jump bsbbif_10_t	|	false: jump bsbbif_11_f
bsbbif_10_t:
	dispose(seq_rxn6[0])
bsbbif_11_f:
	PHI seq_rxn7 = {seq_rxn6,seq_rxn}
	REPEAT_102[0] = REPEAT_101[0] - 1
	jump: bsbbr_8_h
bsbbr_12_f:
	dispose(seq_rxn2[0])
	NOP

numeric_mismatches.note: The paper demonstrates bead-concentration stability over 799 wash cycles (Figure S-2, panels G-I); the script models only a representative 5-cycle wash loop since BioScript has no droplet-split primitive to exactly reproduce the merge/split wash mechanism at scale.

numeric_mismatches.field: repeat 10 times { dATP, dCTP, dGTP, dTTP }
numeric_mismatches.note: This is a generic, illustrative cyclic A/C/G/T dispensing order; the SI excerpt provided does not give the exact paper-specific nucleotide dispensing order used for the real C. parapsilosis targeted/de novo/split pyrosequencing runs (Figure S-3), only the P6/P6-1 control sequences used in solution-phase experiments (Figure S-1).

Detection in the paper is real-time bioluminescence (photons/sec from the luciferase reaction), not a fluorogenic signal; 'detect fluorescence' is used only because it is the sole detect primitive exposed by BioScript's grammar, standing in for the generic quantitative light-emission readout.
This is an illustrative background/no-incorporation cutoff modeling the paper's 'bkgd' calls (Figure S-3), not an exact photon-count threshold stated in the text.

The actual pyrosequencing enzyme cocktail (ATP sulfurylase, luciferase, apyrase, APS, luciferin) is not itemized as separate reagents in the provided SI excerpt; it is modeled here as a single combined 'enzyme_mix' manifest for simplicity.

metadata.notes: This protocol details Droplet-Based Pyrosequencing Using Digital Microfluidics (on-chip PCR amplification, magnetic-bead-based purification, and cyclic dNTP pyrosequencing with real-time luminescence detection). The assay is performed on a Digital Microfluidics (DMF) platform. Key reagents used in the assay include Genomic DNA and Primer Mix.
